references.text: The Lord explains that the people are too many and that He will reduce their number so that Israel may not boast in themselves
Gideon and the 300 men carry out the attack against the Midianites with torches and horns, and the Lord gives them victory
Jonathan expresses similar confidence that the Lord can save by many or by few
Isaiah prophesies that only a remnant will turn back, even though the people are as numerous as the sand of the sea
Describes the Midianite army as numbering 135,000 men and shows how miraculous the victory with just 300 men was
A king is not saved by his great army, confirming that victory comes from the Lord, not from numbers
Moses warns Israel against thinking that their own strength has given them victory, a theme central to the story of Gideon
